Package org.smtlib

Class SolverResolver

java.lang.Object
org.smtlib.SolverResolver
public final class SolverResolver extends Object
For internal use only (public so that the tests can reach it); not part of the API. Resolves a solver name, from the merged jsmtlib.properties, to the adapter class and the executable or command that SMT.Configuration.createSolver(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) constructs it with (#123). The platform, solver directory and class lookup are passed in, so that the rules can be tested with no solver installed.

    • resolve

      public static SolverResolver.Resolution resolve(Properties props, String solvername, String executable, String platform, String solverDir, Function<String,Class<?>> classLookup) throws ISolver.CreationException
      Resolves the solver:
      1. the adapter: a .adapter.<platform> property, then .adapter; else the class Solver_<name> (with - and . in the name as _); else, for a z3 name, Solver_z3_recent; else Solver_smt;
      2. a .command property, split at commas, if given;
      3. the executable: the one given, else .exec.<platform>, then .exec; resolved by SMT.resolveExecutablePath(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), and put in the command in place of %exec%, or as its first element if there is no %exec%; with neither a command nor an executable, the solver name itself, resolved the same way.
      The test pseudo-solver is Solver_test, with the executable as given.
      Parameters:
      props - the merged properties, or null for none
      solvername - the name of the solver
      executable - the caller's executable, or null to resolve one
      platform - the platform name, as SMT.platformName() gives it
      solverDir - the solver directory (SMT_SOLVER_DIR), or null
      classLookup - the class with a given name, or null if there is none
      Throws:
      ISolver.CreationException - if the .command property has no content

    • configuredExecutable

      public static String configuredExecutable(Properties props, String solvername, String platform)
      The executable the properties configure for the solver: .exec.<platform>, then .exec; null if neither is given, or it is blank. A platform-specific override is for solvers whose executable filename itself differs by platform (e.g. z3-4.3 ships as z3-4.3.1 on Unix/macOS but z3-4.3.2 on Windows). Not resolved to a path.
